# spec/source/path

`spec/source/path` — where a contract's source is read from, and the
refusal of a file that is not spec text.

A source is located by its `path` (relative to the contract's directory)
or, for an RFC given by number, by looking for rfc&lt;n&gt;.xml then rfc&lt;n&gt;.txt
beside the contract, in ../rfcs, then in the root's rfcs/. The root is
where vector is installed (sourceInstallRoot), for every command, whatever
the current directory. Its `file` does
not locate it: it records which file was read (sourceLabel), and a check
refuses a contract whose `file` names another.

A contract can come from anyone, so it may read only spec text: a file
beside it, or under specs/ or rfcs/ beside it, beside its parent, or in the
root, with no hidden directory below that and no specs/ or rfcs/ that is
itself a symbolic link (which could lead anywhere). The file is judged after
every link is followed, opened, and judged again as the file the descriptor
holds, and its bytes come from that descriptor: a link swapped between the
judgement and the read cannot change what is read.

Generated from [src/spec/source/path.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/source/path.ts).

## Declarations

### sourceInstallRoot

Where vector is installed, whose rfcs/ and specs/ sources are read from by
every command that reads a contract: the directory above the running
binary when that binary lives in a `dist/` (`<root>/dist/vector`), else the
current directory (a test program built elsewhere, say).

```ts
function sourceInstallRoot(): string
```

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the root

</scalar-field>

### sourceRfcPlaces

The places an RFC given only by number is looked for, nearest first: beside
the contract, in ../rfcs, then in the root's rfcs/; at each the XML before
the plain text, since the XML is an RFC's definitive form.

```ts
function sourceRfcPlaces(n: i32, contractPath: string, root: string): string[]
```

<scalar-field name="n" type="i32" required>

the RFC's number

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="contractPath" type="string" required>

the contract's own path

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="root" type="string" required>

the root whose rfcs/ is searched last

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[]">

the candidate paths, in the order they are tried

</scalar-field>

### sourceCandidate

The file a source is read from, before it is judged: its `path` beside the
contract, else the first of sourceRfcPlaces that exists and that a reader
reads (so an rfc&lt;n&gt;.xml with no XML reader falls back to the .txt),
preferring the one its recorded `file` names exactly, then one with that
file's name (an rfc&lt;n&gt;.xml added later must not displace the file the
contract was checked against).

```ts
function sourceCandidate(
  decl: SourceDecl,
  contractPath: string,
  root: string,
  exts: string[],
): Result<string, string>
```

<scalar-field name="decl" type="SourceDecl" required>

the source

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="contractPath" type="string" required>

the contract's own path

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="root" type="string" required>

the root whose rfcs/ is searched last

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="exts" type="string[]" required>

the extensions a reader is registered for, with their dots

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;string, string&gt;">

`Ok` with the path to read, or `Err` when a name is refused
  (sourceNameProblem), the RFC is on disk nowhere, or it names nothing

</scalar-field>

### sourceRoots

The directories a contract may read spec text under: its own (real)
directory, and specs/ and rfcs/ of that directory's parent, of its
grandparent, and of the root, leaving out any specs/ or rfcs/ that is a
symbolic link.

```ts
function sourceRoots(contractPath: string, root: string): string[]
```

<scalar-field name="contractPath" type="string" required>

the contract's own path

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="root" type="string" required>

the root whose specs/ and rfcs/ are allowed too

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[]">

real absolute directories

</scalar-field>

### sourcePathProblem

Why a contract may not read the file at `real` (a resolved path) as a
source: it is under none of sourceRoots, or a directory below its root
starts with "." (.git, .ssh).

```ts

  decl: SourceDecl,
  shown: string,
  real: string,
  contractPath: string,
  root: string,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="decl" type="SourceDecl" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="shown" type="string" required>

<scalar-field name="real" type="string" required>

<scalar-field name="root" type="string" required>

### sourceLabel

How a source's `file` names the file at `real`: its path under specs/ or
rfcs/ of the root or of the contract's directory or an ancestor, the
shortest such (rfcs/rfc4648.txt wherever the contract sits); else, for a
file below the contract's directory, its path from the directory holding
that one (contracts/x.txt).

```ts
function sourceLabel(
  real: string,
  contractPath: string,
  root: string,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="real" type="string" required>

the resolved path of the file read

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="contractPath" type="string" required>

the contract's own path

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="root" type="string" required>

the root whose specs/ and rfcs/ name files too

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

the label, or null when no `file` can name it

</scalar-field>

### sourceReadConfined

Reads a source's file if it is spec text (sourcePathProblem). The path is
judged once resolved, opened, and judged again as the file the descriptor
holds (/proc/self/fd), and the bytes are read from that descriptor, so a
link or directory swapped in between cannot change what is read. A FIFO, a
device or a directory is refused before a byte is read.

```ts
function sourceReadConfined(
  decl: SourceDecl,
  candidate: string,
  contractPath: string,
  root: string,
): Result<SourceRead, string>
```

<scalar-field name="decl" type="SourceDecl" required>

the source

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="candidate" type="string" required>

the path to read (sourceCandidate)

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="contractPath" type="string" required>

the contract's own path

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="root" type="string" required>

the root whose specs/ and rfcs/ are allowed too

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;SourceRead, string&gt;">

`Ok` with what was read, or `Err` with why it was not

</scalar-field>
